citation.source: Dalla Man C, Raimondo DM, Rizza RA, Cobelli C. GIM, simulation software of meal glucose-insulin model. J Diabetes Sci Technol. 2007; and the curated SBML, BioModels BIOMD0000000379
citation.locator: GIM: "45 g of glucose is ingested at 8 a.m., 70 g at noon, and 70 g at 8 p.m."; SBML: meal dose D = 78000 mg. The range spans the meal sizes the model's authors simulated; it is not a formal validation range.

citation.source: Dalla Man C, Raimondo DM, Rizza RA, Cobelli C. GIM, simulation software of meal glucose-insulin model. J Diabetes Sci Technol. 2007
citation.locator: "peripheral and hepatic insulin sensitivity (V_max and k_p3 in model, respectively)"; "peripheral and hepatic insulin sensitivity, which are set to 30% of the normal". V_max read as the whole maximum uptake rate, V_m0 + V_mX (named V_mmax in the curated SBML).

citation.source: Engeroff T, Groneberg DA, Wilke J. After dinner rest a while, after supper walk a mile? A systematic review with meta-analysis on the acute postprandial glycemic response to exercise before and after meal ingestion in healthy subjects and patients with impaired glucose tolerance. Sports Med. 2023;53(4):849-869
citation.locator: Post-meal exercise started 0–29 min or 30–120 min after the meal; the effect was greatest within 30 min of finishing the meal.

citation.source: Romeres D, Schiavon M, Basu A, Cobelli C, Basu R, Dalla Man C. Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab. 2021;321(1):E122-E129
citation.locator: Exercise lasted 1 hour at 65% VO2max; the effect sizes used come from that protocol, so longer activity is outside what was measured.
